messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: prod - High GPU pool saturation impacting /v1/generate — error rate spike observed (12% -> 7xx/errors), latency p50/p95 rising. Paging on-call.
ashley: ack, seeing the page. pulling metrics now. queue depth looks high. I’ll post quick numbers.
ashley: quick dump:
```
kubectl -n inference get hpa generate
NAME      REFERENCE           TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
generate  Deployment/generate  120%/80%  2         50        32
```
ryan: whoa replicas 32. what’s node/GPU saturation?
infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale_up request accepted, pool allocation delayed due to GPU warmup. reason: warmup_pending (image_pull+init).
mai: confirmed - gpu-pool-prod-usw shows 100% GPU utilization across nodes, 6 pending pods in NodeProvisioner queue.
lena: customers reporting timeouts. @ashley can you estimate affected requests in last 10m?
ashley: from router metrics: 10m window -> 4.6k requests to /v1/generate, errors 560, queue latency median 800ms -> tail 8.2s. impact: some enterprise customers seeing throttles.
ryan: hypothesis 1: HPA triggered additional replicas but GPU pool couldn't supply nodes fast enough (warmup delay) -> backlog grew, causing router-level queueing and timeouts.
mai: hypothesis 2: a recent image push increased container start time (delta +90s) which amplified warmup delays. checking image build timestamps.
ashley: logs: node-provisioner shows backoff loops: 
```
2026-03-15T03:21:17Z provisioner: launching instance g4dn.xlarge-123
2026-03-15T03:22:48Z provisioner: image pull 90s for inference-runtime:prod-2026-03-14
2026-03-15T03:24:12Z node ready, kubelet registration
2026-03-15T03:24:20Z pod generate-xxx scheduled but entering init (kv-cache-warmup)
```
lena: that kv-cache-warmup step is expected but should be async. is the init container blocking?
ashley: yes, current PodSpec uses initContainer that preloads model shards into local SSD, blocks main container start — not async.
ryan: quick mitigation options: 1) scale up a spare warm pool (if available) 2) change rollout to use a smaller init (hot-start) image 3) divert traffic to prod-eu as temporary fallback.
mai: warm pool status: 0 spare nodes. last night maintenance drained a subset. we can request emergency capacity from cloud (ETA ~6-8m).
ashley: implementing temporary traffic diversion: routing rule change to split 30% traffic to prod-eu for /v1/generate can reduce load. Doing a canary shift now.
ashley: /ops run: 
```
# routing patch
curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/routes -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","split":{"prod-usw":70,"prod-eu":30}}'
```
infra-bot: routing change applied, traffic split 70/30.
ryan: monitoring queue depth and error rate now.
ashley: updated metrics after split (2m): requests 10m rolling -> errors down to 180 (from 560), p95 latency down to 3.2s. queue depth decreased ~45%.
mai: still seeing a few init failures on new pods: image pull rate limit warnings in registry logs. possible artifact of increased replica churn.
lena: customer-impact note: Support reports 4 enterprise customers (<1% of accounts) saw degraded QPS and retried. Not yet SLA breach but close. tagging for post-incident follow-up.
ryan: timeline so far: 
- 03:20 incident-bot: error rate spike detected
- 03:21 HPA scaled to 32 replicas as auto response
- 03:21-03:24 NodeProvisioner spinning up instances; image pulls + init container increased start time (~90-150s)
- 03:24 6 pods pending due to node allocation / registry throttling
- 03:28 routing shift 30% -> prod-eu applied
- 03:30 errors and tail latencies decreasing
ashley: adding debugging artifacts to thread: link to metrics: https://metrics.internal/d/abcd/generate-overview?from=now-15m&to=now
mailed: creating ticket INF-6452 to track registry rate limits and warm pool sizing.
mai: hypothesis 3: HPA corset: HPA target threshold at 80% CPU for generate might be too aggressive given GPU-bound workloads — it triggered too late/overreacted. we should examine using custom metric (queue-depth) instead.
ryan: agree, queue-depth would be a stronger signal. add to RCA.
lena: on-call handoff in 30m. @ryan are you able to take next shift?
ryan: I can take the handoff. Ashley — any outstanding tasks?
ashley: summary for handoff -> mitigation applied: traffic split 70/30, emergency cloud capacity requested (ETA 6-8m), tracking registry pull errors, created INF-6452. Current status: error rate down, queue depth slowly falling, warm pool still 0. Next actions: monitor until node provisioning completes and new pods pass readiness; then revert route split.
ryan: thanks. I’ll watch metrics and coordinate with cloud team for capacity. If anything regresses, re-escalate page.
ashley: handing off. good night, folks.
incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff recorded - ashley -> ryan at 03:40 UTC.
ryan: taking over monitoring. will post when we have full pool capacity and readiness.
infra-bot: autoscaler event stream (excerpt):
```
[03:25:10] scale_request accepted -> provisioning 4 nodes
[03:30:50] image_pull_rate_limited for 2 instances
[03:35:22] node_ready for g4dn.xlarge-456
[03:37:10] pods warming kv-cache (init) - expected 60s
[03:39:45] pods ready and receiving traffic
```
ryan: current ask for RCA: collect: HPA metrics (replica history), node provisioner logs, registry slowdowns, pod init durations, router queue-time series. I’ll start assembling timeline doc. tagging @mai @lena for logs.
mai: will attach node and registry logs to the INF-6452 ticket.
lena: I’ll coordinate customer comms with support, prepare a short note if SLA threshold crossed.
ryan: ok, closing active mitigation. leaving thread open for RCA artifacts and final postmortem.
